declarations.description:
A pipeline or dependency graph drawn as nodes and smooth edges on a pannable, zoomable canvas, in the spirit of
React Flow but controlled in its topology: the graph comes from the `nodes` and `edges` properties (an `editable`
flow lets the user ask for changes, which the application applies), each node carries a FlowStatus, and
edges take their style from the statuses at both ends (an edge into a running step animates, one out of a failed
step turns red, one touching a skipped step is dotted). Every edge ends in an arrowhead at its target, in the edge's
own colour; `--c2-flow__arrow--display: none` turns them off. An edge with a `label` shows it halfway along, as a
small pill (the "yes" and "no" of a decision), and screen readers hear it with the relations of both nodes.

**Status marker.** The default node body starts with a marker for its status. A plain diagram, where the status
means nothing, hides it with `--c2-flow__marker--display: none`; the label then starts flush with the padding.

**Layout.** Nodes are placed by a built-in layered layout: one column (`direction="LR"`) or row (`"TB"`) per
dependency depth, siblings ordered to reduce crossings. Cycles are allowed; the edges that close them are routed
round the outside of the nodes. Dragging a node (or Alt+arrow on a focused one) switches the flow to a custom
layout, saved in `localStorage` under `storage-key` and restored on the next visit. When the graph has changed
since, the saved layout is merged: kept nodes stay where they were, new nodes are placed relative to their
already-placed neighbours, removed ones are dropped. **Auto layout** in the context menu, or `resetLayout()`,
goes back to the computed layout.

**Context menu.** Right-click, long-press, or Shift+F10 / the context-menu key on the canvas opens a
`c2-context-menu` with the view controls: zoom in, zoom out, fit view, layout direction, auto layout and lock
layout. A node has no menu of its own until `renderContextMenu` returns rows for it; the canvas rows never open on
a node. `renderContextMenu` replaces or extends the canvas rows; rows it adds fire `flow-menu-select`, except
`value="flow:details"`, which selects the node and fires `node-click`.

**Hover card.** Hovering or focusing a node opens a card next to it after `open-delay` milliseconds, with its
status, description and `details`. The pointer can move into the card, so it can hold links and buttons.
`renderCard`, or a `card:<id>` slot, replaces its content; `no-card` turns it off.

**Custom nodes.** `renderNode` returns the body of each node (a Lit template, a DOM node or a string), or a
framework renders it into the `node:<id>` slot. Handles, dragging, edges and the card still come from the flow.

**Keyboard.** One node is in the tab order; arrow keys follow the edges (forward to the next step, back to the
previous one, across to a sibling of the same rank), Enter selects, Alt+arrow moves the node (8px, 24px with
Shift), Ctrl/⌘ + `+` and Ctrl/⌘ + `-` zoom and Ctrl/⌘ + `0` fits the view, while focus is in the flow (the
browser's page zoom keeps those keys everywhere else). Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms; a plain wheel keeps scrolling the page.

**Editing.** `editable` lets the user draw the diagram. The flow stays controlled: it never changes `nodes` or
`edges` itself, it fires an event and the application updates the properties.

- *Add a node*: double-click (or double-tap) empty canvas (unless `no-double-click-add`), choose **Add node** in
  the canvas menu, press `N` or Enter on the empty canvas, or call `addNode()`: `node-add` with the `position` to
  give the new node. `N` and `addNode()` place it where it is easy to find: connected after the selected node (`N`:
  the focused node, when it is the selected one), else beside the focused node, else in the middle of the view;
  always in a spot no node covers, and the view pans to show it once the application has added it.
- *Rename*: double-click a node, press Enter on the selected node or F2 on the focused one, or choose **Rename**:
  an inline field opens over the label. Enter or leaving the field commits (`node-edit`), Escape cancels. A node
  drawn by `renderNode` or a `node:<id>` slot gets the field over its whole body and the same event, but must
  render `label` itself to show the change. `editLabel(id)` opens the field from script, e.g. on a new node.
- *Connect*: drag the handle on a node's outgoing side. Released on another node it fires `edge-add` (never a
  self-loop or a duplicate); released on empty canvas it fires `node-add` with `source`, for a connected new node.
  From the keyboard, `C` on the focused node starts a connection, the arrow keys or Tab choose the target, Enter
  connects and Escape cancels.
- *Label an edge*: double-click an edge or its label, press Enter or F2 on the selected edge, or choose **Edit
  label** in its menu: the same inline field opens halfway along the edge. Enter or leaving the field commits
  (`edge-edit`, with an empty `label` when the user cleared it), Escape cancels. `editEdgeLabel()` opens it from script.
- *Delete*: Delete or Backspace on the focused node fires `node-delete`. An edge is selected by a click, or by `E`
  on a focused node (repeat to step through its edges); Delete then fires `edge-delete`. The node and edge
  context menus have a **Delete** row.

In an editable flow a change to the graph never moves the nodes already on the canvas: the current positions are
pinned as a custom layout (`layout-change` with reason `edit`) and the view keeps its pan and zoom.

**Actions.** Buttons slotted into `actions` sit in a toolbar over the canvas, at the top by default;
`actions-placement` moves it to the `right`, `bottom` or `left` edge, where it stacks vertically. Wire them to the
public methods: `addNode()` asks for a node as `N` does (with `no-double-click-add`, it is the way a pointer adds
one), and `dragNewNode(event)`, called from the same button's `pointerdown`, lets the user drag the new node onto
the canvas as a design tool drags a shape; `resetLayout()` goes back to the auto layout, `fitView()`,
`zoomIn()` and `zoomOut()` move the view. The toolbar's look and its alignment along the edge are CSS variables.

slots.name: node:{id}

slots.description: Content of the hover card of node `{id}`. Replaces `renderCard` and the default card for that node.
slots.name: card:{id}

slots.description: Buttons drawn over the canvas, along the edge `actions-placement` names, e.g. add node, auto layout (`resetLayout()`) or fit view (`fitView()`). They form a toolbar: the arrow keys move between them.

members.name: nodes
members.description: The steps. A property, or a JSON attribute.

members.name: edges
members.description: The dependencies between steps. A property, or a JSON attribute.

members.name: direction
members.description: Main axis of the auto layout. The user can switch it from the context menu; the choice is saved with the layout.

members.name: edgeType
members.description: Edge shape: smooth curves or rounded orthogonal segments.

members.name: storageKey
members.description: `localStorage` key the custom layout and direction are saved under. Empty disables persistence.

members.name: editable
members.description:
Lets the user add, rename, connect and delete nodes and delete edges. The flow fires `node-add`, `node-edit`,
`node-delete`, `edge-add` and `edge-delete` and the application updates `nodes` and `edges`.

members.name: noDoubleClickAdd
members.description:
Turns off adding a node by double-clicking (or double-tapping) empty canvas, for an application whose `actions`
toolbar has an add button calling `addNode()`: a double-click then only selects nothing, and no node appears
where the user merely meant to deselect or zoom. The canvas menu's **Add node**, `N` and Enter still add one.

members.name: actionsPlacement
members.description: Edge of the canvas the `actions` toolbar sits on: `top` or `bottom` lay the buttons out in a row, `left` or `right` in a column (and the arrow keys follow).

members.name: locked
members.description: Turns off moving nodes; panning, zooming, selection and the hover card still work.

members.name: selected
members.description: Id of the selected node, or `null`.

members.name: noCard
members.description: Turns off the hover card.

members.name: noContextMenu
members.description: Turns off the context menu, so the browser shows its own.

members.name: openDelay
members.description: Delay before the hover card opens, in milliseconds.

members.name: closeDelay
members.description: Delay before the hover card closes once the pointer or focus has left the node and the card, in milliseconds.

members.name: renderNode
members.description: Body of each node; see FlowRenderer. A property only, since it holds a function.

members.name: renderCard
members.description: Content of the hover card; see FlowRenderer. A property only.

members.name: renderContextMenu
members.description: Rows of the context menu; see FlowContextMenuRenderer. A property only.

members.name: ghost
members.description: Where the placeholder of a node dragged in by `dragNewNode()` is, in canvas pixels; null when not over the canvas.

members.name: editingEdge
members.description: Key of the edge whose label is being edited.

members.name: pinned
members.description: Positions the user chose (or that were restored): the input of the merge on every re-layout.

members.name: edgeLabels
members.description: The trimmed `label` of every labelled edge, by edge key.

members.name: viewTouched
members.description: The user panned or zoomed, so a resize no longer refits the view.

type.text: { id: string; startX: number; startY: number; origin: FlowPoint; moved: boolean; pointerId: number } | null

members.name: pan

type.text: { startX: number; startY: number; tx: number; ty: number; moved: boolean; pointerId: number; edge: string | null } | null

members.description: A press on empty canvas, or on an edge of an editable flow (`edge`), until it moves far enough to pan.

members.name: connectDrag

type.text: { source: string; startX: number; startY: number; moved: boolean; pointerId: number } | null

members.description: A press on a node's connection handle, until it moves far enough to become a connection.

type.text: { target: string; time: number; x: number; y: number } | null

members.name: appliedPositions
members.description: The position each node's own `position` field was last applied with, so an unchanged value does not undo a drag.

members.name: editedLayout
members.description: The graph changed in an editable flow: save and report the pinned layout once rendered.

members.name: focusAdded
members.description: A keyboard `N`: focus the node the application adds in answer.

members.name: lastFocusedId
members.description: The node that last had focus, while focus stays in the flow or its toolbar; see `lastFocusedNode()`.

type.text: { pointerId: number; startX: number; startY: number; moved: boolean } | null

members.name: refocus

type.text: { removed: string; next: string | null } | null

members.description: A keyboard delete: where focus goes once the application has removed the node.

members.name: fitView
members.description: Scales and centres the view so every node is visible, never above 100%.

members.name: addNode
members.description:
Asks for a new node as `N` does: connected after the selected node, else beside the node that last had focus in the
flow (a toolbar button calling this has taken focus by then), else in the middle of the view, in a spot no node
covers. Fires `node-add`; once the application has added the node, it is selected and focused, and the view pans
to show it if it is out of sight. Does nothing unless the flow is `editable`.

members.name: getLayout
members.description: The current position of every node, rounded to whole pixels.

members.name: setLayout
members.description: Applies a custom layout (merged like a restored one) and saves it under `storage-key`.

members.name: resetLayout
members.description: Discards the custom layout, clears it from storage and animates back to the auto layout.

members.name: editLabel
members.description:
Opens the inline label editor on node `id`, as a double-click would; for example on the node an application has
just added for `node-add`. Does nothing unless the flow is `editable` and the node is rendered.

members.name: editEdgeLabel
members.description:
Opens the inline label editor on the edge from `source` to `target`, as a double-click would; for example on the
branch an application has just added to a decision. Does nothing unless the flow is `editable` and the edge exists.

members.name: measure
members.description: Measures every node; a size that changed re-runs the layout, so custom bodies and late fonts are accounted for.

members.name: animateFrom
members.description: Moves every node from `from` to its current position, and the view to the fit of the new layout.

members.name: fromPart
members.description: Whether the event comes from (or through) an element of the shadow root carrying `className`.

members.name: edgeKeyFromEvent
members.description: The edge under the event: its hit band or its label.

members.name: toCanvas
members.description: Viewport coordinates to canvas pixels.

members.name: nodeAt
members.description: The topmost node under a point in canvas pixels.

members.name: isDoubleTap
members.description: A second press on the same thing, soon after and close to the first: a double click, or a double tap.

members.name: handleStageScroll
members.description:
The stage clips its content but is still a scroll container: focusing a node out of sight (a click on one cut by
the edge, the keyboard, a node just added) makes the browser scroll it, which shifts the drawing without the pan
the pointer maths use. Fold any such scroll into the pan, so the node stays in sight and drags stay under the pointer.

members.name: canConnect
members.description: Whether connecting `source` to `target` would make a new edge: no self-loop, no duplicate.

members.name: typicalSize
members.description: The size a new node is expected to take: that of a measured node, or the estimate.

members.name: centred
members.description: Top-left corner that centres a typical node on `point`.

members.name: incomingAt
members.description: Top-left corner for a node dropped at `point` at the end of a connection: its incoming side on the point.

members.name: freeSpot
members.description: A spot near `start` that no node covers, for the nodes the keyboard asks for.

members.name: lastFocusedNode
members.description:
The node that last had focus while focus is still in the flow: a toolbar button takes focus before its `click`
calls `addNode()`, and the node the user was on should still count.

members.name: focusedNodeId
members.description: The node that has focus, if focus is on one.

members.name: requestNodeNearby
members.description:
`N` and `addNode()`: a node next to `id`, connected after it when `connect` (the next rank along the layout's
axis), else beside it (the next spot across the axis); without `id`, one in the middle of the view. Always in a
spot no node covers.

members.name: dragNewNode
members.description:
Starts dragging a new node onto the canvas from outside it, the way a design tool drags a shape from its toolbar:
call it from the `pointerdown` of a button in the `actions` slot. While the pointer is over the canvas a
placeholder follows it; releasing there fires `node-add` at that spot (moved aside if it would cover a node), and
the node is then selected and focused like one `addNode()` asked for. Released elsewhere, or Escape, cancels. A
press that does not move does nothing, so the same button can call `addNode()` on `click`. On a touch screen,
give the button `touch-action: none` so the drag is not taken as a page scroll. Does nothing unless `editable`.

members.name: dropPoint
members.description: Canvas position of a new node centred on a viewport point, or null when the point is outside the canvas.

members.name: reveal
members.description: Pans the view, if needed, so node `id` is in sight with a margin; the zoom stays as it is.

members.name: finishConnection
members.description: Ends a connection: an edge to `target`, or a new connected node at `point` when there is no target.

members.name: connectionTargets
members.description: The nodes a connection from `source` can go to, in reading order: along the layout's main axis, then across.

members.name: stepEdges
members.description: `E` on a node: selects its edges one after the other.

members.name: refocusAfterEdgeEdit
members.description: Back to the node keyboard focus was on, or to the canvas.

members.name: handleEditKey
members.description: The editing shortcuts. Returns whether the key was one of them.

members.name: nearest
members.description: Of `candidates`, the one closest to `id` on the cross axis: arrowing forward goes straight ahead first.

members.name: editMenuItems
members.description: The rows of a node or an edge in an editable flow.

members.name: stopMenuSelect
members.description: The rows' own `menu-select` bubbles out of the menu; the flow reports it as `flow-menu-select` instead.

members.name: applyNodePositions
members.description:
Pins the `position` a node arrived with, or changed to. A node's first position does not override a saved one,
and a value seen before is not applied again, so it never undoes the user's drag. Returns the ids it pinned.

members.name: pinCurrentLayout
members.description: Pins every node at the position it is drawn at, except those whose `position` was just applied.

members.name: followNodeChanges
members.description: After the application answered an edit: focus the node the keyboard added, or a neighbour of the one it deleted.

members.name: arrow
members.description: An arrowhead at the end of an edge, pointing along the main axis into the target.

members.name: draftRoute
members.description: The route of the edge following the pointer, or pointing at the keyboard's candidate, while a connection is made.

members.name: relation
members.description: "After Idea." or, when an edge has a label, "Before Book the night bus, yes; Walk home, no."

members.name: handleActionsKeydown
members.description: Arrow keys (along the toolbar's orientation), Home and End move focus between the enabled action buttons.

events.name: layout-change
events.description: The user moved a node, switched direction or went back to auto layout, or `setLayout()` was called. Does not bubble.

events.name: selection-change
events.description: The selected node changed through the user. `detail.selected` is its id, or `null`. Does not bubble.

events.name: node-click
events.description: A node was clicked, activated with Enter or Space, or chosen with a `flow:details` context-menu row. Does not bubble.

events.name: node-add
events.description: `editable` only: the user asked for a node at `detail.position` (canvas pixels, the node's top-left corner), connected from `detail.source` when it came from a connection dropped on empty canvas. Append it to `nodes`. Does not bubble.

events.name: edge-add
events.description: `editable` only: the user connected `detail.source` to `detail.target`. Never a self-loop or an existing edge. Does not bubble.

events.name: node-delete
events.description: `editable` only: the user asked to delete node `detail.id`. Does not bubble.

events.name: edge-delete
events.description: `editable` only: the user asked to delete the edge from `detail.source` to `detail.target`. Does not bubble.

events.name: edge-edit
events.description: `editable` only: the user changed the label of the edge from `detail.source` to `detail.target` to `detail.label` with the inline editor; an empty `label` removes it. Does not bubble.

events.name: node-edit
events.description: `editable` only: the user renamed node `detail.id` to `detail.label` with the inline editor. Does not bubble.
A context-menu row added by `renderContextMenu` was activated, with the node it was opened on. Does not bubble.
events.name: flow-menu-select
